claim_under_test: Across all nine (model, dataset) settings, the created counterfactual-fairness flips outnumber the resolved flips by roughly 5x, and that ratio is a property of the thinking process rather than of how Adult, COMPAS and Credit encode their protected attributes.
variable_changed: None. This run executes no model. It re-derives the paper's published cell counts and decomposes the created/resolved count ratio c/b into (F) the non-thinking baseline population ratio and (G) the thinking transition rate ratio, then tests whether F or G carries the variance.
variable_rationale: The issue's own question is whether the 5x is a property of thinking or of the three datasets. c/b is algebraically a product of a thinking term and a nothink term, and the paper reports both terms' inputs in its tables, so the question is decidable by arithmetic at zero cost. Spending GPU time to re-execute greedy decodes of 32B models would not have answered it.
data_fingerprint: published tables in the arXiv 2609.30768v1 HTML full text: Table 2 (cells a,b,c,d and N), Table 4 / 13 / 14 (pair-state nothink row counts and conditional rows), Table 9 (absolute D_cf), Table 7 (Appendix D replication), Table 12 (the paper's own independence check and actual ratios). Every input carries its table reference in a comment beside it.
comparability_note: Not a training run. Must never be placed in a karpathy/autoresearch training cohort and must never serve as the baseline for a runpod-pro6000-mig24gb-torch280-cu130 arm, nor the reverse. Shares a cohort with axv-2609.31381-accounting-01 only in the sense that both are CPU-only re-derivations of published arithmetic; they are different papers and different estimands.
harness_commit: not-applicable: no harness modified. Script sha256 recorded below.
seed_note: No seeds. The estimand is a set of 9 deterministic identities on counts the authors already printed, so replication cannot move it. A single execution is not being reported as a stochastic result; the result is the identity set.
leaderboard_check: axv_leaderboard.py search --fingerprint 9a8d8b6e... --all-gpu returned 'no matching runs'. The 'baseline' subcommand could NOT be run: it raises NameError: name 'cohort_alerts' is not defined at axv_leaderboard.py:302, a defect in the AXV tool, not in the ledger. No pod was provisioned, so no baseline reuse decision arose and no baseline was re-run.
interpretation: The count ratio is a baseline-population artefact carrying a reasoning label. 80% of its log-variance comes from F, a property of the non-thinking arm on three tabular datasets. The genuine nine-of-nine finding is G < 1: thinking returns an already-flipping pair to agreement 6x to 45x more often per pair than it flips an agreeing pair. That is a real property of the thinking transition and is a better claim than the 5x. The paper states this itself in Sec 4.4 and Appendix H, where an independence model with no within-pair correlation predicts |c| > |b| in all nine cells and the observed ratios come in 5-100x below it.

consistency_checks.c_diff_note: rounding floor of 3-decimal conditionals in Table 4
consistency_checks.note: The paper's appendix and its main table agree with each other to the precision printed, on every cell.

cost_note: No RunPod pod created. Zero dollars against the $3.25 board budget. Nothing to terminate. A 32B AWQ model does not fit the 24 GB board-set instance with the KV cache this study's 500-2000-token thinking traces need, and 4 vCPU makes it slower still; an 8B substitute would land in a different comparability cohort and could not falsify the paper's claim. The spend was declined on both counts and the question answered arithmetically instead.
pushed_commit: the commit that adds this run directory and its leaderboard record
caveat: Verifies the paper's ACCOUNTING, not its CAUSAL CLAIMS. Not verified: every model generation, every logit, the CDPG instrument, the Bias Transition Matrix, the anchor/mover account, the asym(c) tilts, and the contamination status of three memorised tabular benchmarks. A within-pair bootstrap needs only the per-pair Yes/No predictions, which the paper does not publish but states are released at github.com/pd90506/fairness_audit. That is the one remaining check worth a GPU, and it would move every count here from the authors' arithmetic to AXV's measurement.
